summary.text: A redshift is an increase in the wavelength, or a decrease in the frequency, of electromagnetic radiation such as light.
Astronomy has three forms: Doppler redshifts from relative motion, gravitational redshift from radiation escaping gravity, and cosmological redshifts from the universe expanding.
It is written as z, the fractional change in wavelength, and automated redshift surveys help map the large-scale structure of the universe.

facts.label: Cosmic example
facts.value: 3000 K Big Bang radiation became the 3 K microwave background

facts.label: Named after
facts.value: Christian Doppler, who explained it physically in 1842

facts.label: Hubble link
facts.value: In 1929 Hubble related redshift to distance

items.prompt: A galaxy's value of z comes out negative. What does that tell you about its light?

options.label: It is shifted toward longer wavelengths
It is shifted toward shorter wavelengths
It has no wavelength shift at all
Its light has been fully absorbed

items.explain: The value of z is positive for redshifts and negative for blueshifts, which shorten wavelength.

items.prompt: Light climbs out of a region of very strong gravity and arrives at a longer wavelength. Which form of redshift is this?

options.label: Doppler redshift
Cosmological redshift
Observational redshift
Gravitational redshift

items.explain: Gravitational redshift occurs as radiation escapes from gravitational potentials.

items.prompt: The microwave background today is far colder than the glow it started as. What explains that?

options.label: The radiation was gradually absorbed by passing stars
The radiation was blueshifted by the early universe's gravity
The original radiation has been redshifted down to long wavelengths
The glow was only ever a cold signal from the start

items.explain: The initial 3000 K radiation from the Big Bang has redshifted far down to become the 3 K cosmic microwave background.

items.prompt: In 1929 Hubble combined his estimated distances to galaxies with Slipher's and Humason's measurements of shifted light. What did he report?

options.label: An approximate link between how far a galaxy is and its redshift
A proof that galaxies never move at all
A list of galaxies sorted by their colour
A formula for how stars burn their fuel

items.explain: Hubble reported an approximate relationship between redshift and distance, now called Hubble's law.

items.prompt: An early proposal said light simply grows tired on its long trip, causing cosmological redshift. What counts against it?

options.label: Light has never been seen to cross space at all
Redshifts are always the same for every distance
Doppler radar never shows any wavelength change
Time-stretching seen in type Ia supernovae observations

items.explain: Zwicky's tired light model has largely been ruled out by timescale stretch observations in type Ia supernovae.

items.prompt: In the 1960s quasars looked like ordinary blue point sources but had large redshifts. What did later work conclude about them?

options.label: They are nearby stars that are unusually dim
They are very powerful but distant objects
They are galaxies that are moving toward us
They are glitches in the telescope instruments

items.explain: Work in the 1960s concluded that quasars were very powerful but distant astronomical objects.
